amber: Quick heads-up — bringing up amber-embed-small into staging. INT4 per-tensor saved ~2.6x memory but recall@5 on long-tail queries dipped a lot. Posting quick numbers and the eval command.

amber: Numbers (wiki-longtail holdout, 2k queries): fp16 recall@5: 0.791; int8 recall@5: 0.785 (-0.6); int4 per-tensor recall@5: 0.738 (-6.7). Overall avg recall@5 drop: -3.5. Tail (freq<=3) recall@5: fp16 0.662 -> int4 0.583 (-7.9).

jules: Oof. Can you paste the eval command and quant pipeline? Also did you run any calibration?

amber: Eval: ```bash
python eval/recall.py --model amber-embed-small --weights /mnt/models/amber/int4_pt.pth --holdout s3://redwood-evals/wiki_longtail/2k.jsonl --k 5 --sim cosine --normalize true --batch 512
```
Quant: per-tensor symmetric int4 using MSE-min with 5k english anchors (global). No affine correction.

sam: Two quick hypotheses: 1) anchors skewed to frequent tokens so tail dims under-calibrated. 2) per-tensor scheme loses per-dim nuance; try per-channel or small per-dim bias correction.

amber: Agreed. Plan: A) run per-channel int4 (same anchors); B) run per-tensor+affine using 10k stratified anchors (tail-heavy); C) add runtime fallback rule: if query token count <=6 or rare-token flag -> route to int8.

jules: Also add a synthetic adversarial test: randomly drop 20% of context tokens and see swap-rate increase. If int4 amplifies swaps for tail queries, that's bad.

eval-bot: Jobs queued: run_A=1819991234-perchan, run_B=1819991234-affine10k, run_C=1819991234-fallback-canary. Started 1819991400, ETA ~22m. Will post recall@k table, tail-cohort breakdown, and swap-rate plots when done.

amber: If affine10k recovers >4% on tail we can consider int4 with an offline stratified calibration step; otherwise prefer int8 for tail cohorts and offer int4 for head-heavy routes. Will update after results. :mag:
